**Why Rd1:**
- **The divider is unbalanced.** Rd1 and Rd2 should be roughly equal to bias vm at mid-supply (about 0.9 V). With Rd1 = 200 kΩ, the divider alone would put vm near 1.71 V.
- **The DC numbers match.** Assuming vin sits at about 0.9 V, it pulls vm down through R1+R2 (about 10.9 kΩ). Solving that node gives vm ≈ 0.945 V. The op-amp follows vm at DC, so vout ≈ 0.94 V, which matches the measured 0.941 V.
- **The f0 shift fits.** The smaller resistance changes the impedance at vm. That node, together with Cd, shapes the low-frequency edge of the measured bandpass, so the peak moves down to about 18.8 Hz.

**Caveat on the f0 link:** I didn't fully derive how f0 depends on Rd1. The MFB parts (R1, R2, R3, C1, C2) on their own work out to a centre near 45 MHz, not 28 Hz. So the low-frequency peak must come from the Rd/Cd bias network interacting with the source, but I haven't computed it to confirm.
